Science.title: New index links changing ocean food webs to Bermuda's spiny lobster fishery

Science.title: LISA to the rescue: Using light to fix cell division
Science.summary: Cell division is a complex process. At the heart of this complexity is a membraneless organelle called the centrosome, which is made up of more than 200 components. It is responsible for clustering mitotic spindles, threadlike structures needed to separate genetic material. It has long remained unclear which parts of the centrosome are necessary and sufficient for spindle assembly.

Science.title: Under the Microscope: NASA-made material for moon manufacturing

Science.title: AI structure prediction speeds discovery of 'molecular glues' to treat disease

Their approach, published in Nature Communications, has uncovered a new class of molecular glues that could neutralize harmful proteins linked to blood cancers and autoimmune diseases. Science.title: Alien life? Why the possibility of exoplanet LHS 1140b emitting helium gas is so exciting

Science.title: Towering 'sponge' dome in Brazil is the secret source of nearby hot springs
Science.summary: A 2025 satellite photo shows the Caldas Novas dome, a 12-mile-long monolith that towers above the Brazilian state of Goiás. The structure acts as a giant sponge, soaking up water that helps fuel nearby hot springs.

Science.title: Christian amulets preserved Roman traditions of protection
Science.summary: For centuries, the Romans turned to amulets to protect themselves or their surroundings. Research by Ph.D. candidate Patricia Kret shows that this tradition continued into the early days of Christianity.

Science.title: How a new textile fabric could triple production in strawberry plants
Science.summary: A new textile used to cover strawberry plants more than tripled fruit yields in tunnel field tests without harming plant health. The technology could also significantly reduce water and pesticide use in strawberry fields.

Science.title: Molecular simulations reveal how an enzyme's shape guides molecular recognition
Science.summary: Enzymes are often described as molecular machines that recognize and process specific molecules. However, they are not rigid structures. Their shapes can change, affecting how molecules enter, interact with and remain within their active sites.

Science.title: Engineered coating lets mitochondria retain their ability to produce energy
Science.summary: Researchers have coated mitochondria with innovative materials without compromising their function, according to a study by IRCCS Fondazione Istituto Neurologico Carlo Besta (FINCB) and Politecnico di Milano. The research was conducted as part of the BraiNs joint laboratory, inaugurated in 2023.

Science.title: Rethinking liquid hydrogen storage with metal-organic frameworks
Science.summary: Liquid hydrogen (LH₂) is attractive for long-distance energy transport because of its high volumetric energy density. But even well-insulated tanks cannot completely prevent heat from entering. As the liquid warms, hydrogen evaporates and pressure builds, leading to boil-off losses during storage and transport.

Science.title: Light-driven nickel catalyst forms chemical bonds using less metal
Science.summary: Pharmaceuticals, fine chemicals, and agrochemicals are produced industrially using a wide range of chemical reactions. These processes need to become more efficient, less expensive, and more sustainable.

Science.title: One in eight cancers worldwide linked to infections, WHO agency says
Science.summary: A new study from the International Agency for Research on Cancer (IARC) shows that an estimated 2.3 million new cancer cases worldwide in 2024 – about 12% of all new cancer cases – were caused by infections and could be prevented with treatment or vaccines. FRANCE 24's Jennie Shin speaks with the lead author of the study, Dr Gary Clifford, Scientist at the IARC.

Science.title: Genetic audit of wheat: Researchers determine the actual variability of a gene responsible for bread quality
Science.summary: A team at the University of Córdoba (UCO) has reviewed and updated the catalog of versions of the wheat gene GLU-B1, which is responsible for a protein that makes up gluten. The team has also made a collection of wheat representing the gene's true variability available to the research community.

Science.title: New device measures curved mirrors' absolute shape to within 2 nanometers without touching them
Science.summary: Researchers at AIST have developed a device that measures the absolute surface profile of curved optical elements with high precision without touching them.

Science.title: Wild tomatoes still hold the flavor we bred away: New map shows breeders where to look
Science.summary: Modern tomatoes are a breeding success story. Generations of selection have made them bigger, firmer, more productive and easier to ship. But that progress came at a cost. Domestication and breeding reduced much of the crop's genetic diversity, and flavor has proven stubbornly hard to breed back in.

Science.title: NYC delivery workers injured at more than five times national rate under intense labor control by apps, survey finds
Science.summary: More than half of New York City's app-based food delivery workers have been injured on the job, and 40% meet the criteria for severe psychological distress, according to a new study from the CUNY Graduate School of Public Health and Health Policy (CUNY SPH), in partnership with the Worker's Justice Project (WJP).

Science.title: Revisiting a Young Isaac Newton
Science.summary: Isaac Newton is typically portrayed as a solitary scientist with intense focus who was obsessed with power and deeply egotistical. But a new book by Caltech historians Jed Buchwald and Mordechai Feingold takes a deeper look at Newton's life in the two decades leading up to the 1687 publication of his groundbreaking text, Principia Mathematica, when he was 44. Using newly digitized scans of Newton's early writings, Buchwald and Feingold uncover a portrait of the young polymath as a curious and social scholar whose interests were often fleeting.

Science.title: Dyed liquid crystals enable light-only control of optical components
Science.summary: A new technique for controlling optical components with light could help usher in a generation of high-efficiency signal-processing technology that could drive futuristic applications such as holographic video.

Science.title: Mobile crisis response programs get new measures of their impact on police calls
Science.summary: Communities across the country are debating the role mobile crisis response programs can play in emergency response. These programs typically take calls from 911 dispatchers involving mental health, substance use, welfare checks and other situations that do not require a law enforcement response.

Science.title: A new chapter in targeting kinase enzymes in cancer
Science.summary: Nature, Published online: 29 September 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-02776-y Inhibitors of tyrosine kinase enzymes have been a cornerstone in precision cancer treatments. Now, targeted protein degraders could reshape therapeutic options.

Science.summary: A U.K. government minister has urged people in Britain to stock up on essentials to prepare for storms magnified by the record-breaking El Niño. Should Americans heed the same advice?
